# Vendored hgraph core

This package is the Horizon-owned copy of the graph storage, analysis, sync,
dashboard data shaping, text rendering, and command-line implementation from
<https://github.com/AxelDlv00/hgraph>.

Imported revision: `f30b15e8822388085779d6417a83a2e8a07a2473`
(2026-07-27, “Improve sync warning coverage”).

Horizon intentionally does not retain an external `hgraph` dependency. Update
this directory by manually porting reviewed changes from that repository. The
standalone hgraph workspace manifest, web server, and static site are not
included: Horizon owns workspace selection and the dashboard UI, while
`horizon graph` exposes the project graph operations.

Intentional Horizon adaptations are kept during updates: the CLI is mounted
under `horizon graph`, and the dashboard data retains semantic `group` values
used by Horizon's graph view even though standalone hgraph no longer renders
that axis.

Both projects are licensed under Apache-2.0; Horizon's root `LICENSE` applies.

   708	def _upsert(g: Graph, nid: str, *, title: str, type: str, content: str,
   709	            owned: dict, dry_run: bool = False) -> bool:
   710	    """Create the node, or overwrite exactly the owned fields — leaving every
   711	    authored field (origin, tags, status, …) in place, clearing ``stale``, and
   712	    unsetting any owned field that is now empty (e.g. a doc comment removed).
   713	
   714	    Return whether the graph differs from the requested state.  ``dry_run``
   715	    performs the same comparison without writing, which lets ``serve`` detect
   716	    pending sync work using the reconciliation rules themselves.
   717	    """
   718	    clean = {k: v for k, v in owned.items() if v is not None}
   719	    empty = [k for k, v in owned.items() if v is None]
   720	    if g.has_node(nid):
   721	        n = g.get_node(nid)
   722	        changed = n.title != title or n.type != type or n.content != content
   723	        changed |= any(n.meta.get(k) != v for k, v in clean.items())
   724	        changed |= any(k in n.meta for k in ("stale", *empty))
   725	        if changed and not dry_run:
   726	            g.modify_node(nid, title=title, type=type, content=content,
   727	                          set_meta=clean, unset=["stale", *empty])
   728	    else:
   729	        changed = True
   730	        if not dry_run:
   731	            g.add_node(title, type=type, id=nid, content=content, **clean)
   732	    return changed

   563	def _lean_code_lines(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
   564	    """Return a parallel list of ``lines`` with every comment span blanked to
   565	    spaces, preserving length and column positions.
   566	
   567	    Lean's grammar for keywords is context-free of comments, but the graph
   568	    scanner works line-by-line, so a docstring or ``/- … -/`` block whose prose
   569	    happens to begin with ``class``/``def``/``theorem`` used to be parsed as a
   570	    real declaration — inventing ghost nodes like ``class can`` from a sentence
   571	    ``…whether the class can carry a witness…`` (I-0472, I-0613). Blanking
   572	    comments first means only genuine code is scanned for ``namespace``/``end``
   573	    and declarations, while the original lines are still used for the body and
   574	    the ``/-- … -/`` docstring capture. Handles nested ``/- … -/``, doc
   575	    comments (``/-- … -/`` opens the same nesting), and ``--`` line comments;
   576	    string literals are not special-cased (they were not before either)."""
   577	    out: list[str] = []
   578	    depth = 0  # block-comment nesting depth carried across lines
   579	    for line in lines:
   580	        chars = list(line)
   581	        i, n = 0, len(line)
   582	        while i < n:
   583	            pair = line[i:i + 2]
   584	            if depth == 0 and pair == "--":
   585	                for k in range(i, n):     # line comment: blank to end of line
   586	                    chars[k] = " "
   587	                break
   588	            if pair == "/-":
   589	                depth += 1
   590	                chars[i] = chars[i + 1] = " "
   591	                i += 2
   592	                continue
   593	            if pair == "-/" and depth > 0:
   594	                depth -= 1
   595	                chars[i] = chars[i + 1] = " "
   596	                i += 2
   597	                continue
   598	            if depth > 0:
   599	                chars[i] = " "
   600	            i += 1
   601	        out.append("".join(chars))
   602	    return out
